transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith — what brings you in to see me today?

Um… thank you, Dr. Smith. I’m not sure if I’m explaining this properly, but I’ve been feeling a bit unsettled at work. I’m a teacher, and sometimes certain staff emails or the morning announcements feel like they’re… directed at me somehow. Like there’s a message in them about me.

I know that probably sounds odd, and my colleagues have been kind about it—they’ll show me the email went to everyone, or that the announcement was general. But even then, I can’t quite shake the feeling. I thought it might be best to talk to someone before I get too worked up about it.
How long have you been noticing this feeling that emails or announcements are referring to you—days, weeks, or longer?

I suppose it’s been… longer than days. Maybe about four months, if I’m being honest. It hasn’t been constant, and I’ve tried not to make too much of it, but that feeling with the emails or announcements has been around since then.

Over these past four months, have you also noticed changes in your mood—like feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or unusually low—or on the other end, periods of feeling unusually elevated, energetic, or irritable?

Um… I don’t think so, not in any big way. I mean, I get tired and a bit worried about it all sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been hopeless or anything like that. And I haven’t had times where I felt unusually energetic or… high, if that’s what you mean.

I hope that answers it properly.
Aside from that feeling about the emails and announcements, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear, or seen things that others don't see?

Well… yes, a little. I wasn’t sure whether to mention it because it sounds more serious than I mean it to, but sometimes when I’m at home and it’s quiet, or after the classroom has emptied, I hear a woman’s voice.

It’s usually just my name, or a short comment about what I’m doing. It’s clear enough that I’ll sometimes answer before I realize there isn’t anyone there. It doesn’t happen all the time, though. Does that make sense?
Do you have any medical conditions, recent illnesses, head injuries, or are you using any medications, recreational drugs, or alcohol that might be relevant here?

No, I don’t think there’s anything like that, not that I’m aware of. I haven’t had a head injury or anything recent that seems connected.

I’m not using recreational drugs, and alcohol isn’t really a factor for me. Medications… nothing that I can think of that would explain this. I hope that’s the kind of information you mean.

Over these past four months, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your job, keep up with daily responsibilities, or interact with friends and family—compared to before this started?

I’m still working, yes. I’m still teaching my classes, so it’s not as if everything has fallen apart or anything.

But… I suppose compared with before, I’ve needed more help than I’d like to admit. A couple of coworkers have covered parts of project lessons for me, and planning meetings have been harder to get through without someone sort of helping me stay on track.

Outside of school, I’ve become less reliable. I used to be good about book club and theater things and neighborhood events, but lately I’ve canceled or just not followed through. I don’t mean to be difficult. It’s just been harder to keep up. Is that the kind of change you’re asking about?

Have you noticed any changes in how you think or express yourself—like trouble organizing your thoughts, finding it hard to follow conversations, or feeling less motivated or emotionally flat compared to before?

I think… yes, somewhat. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I do still care about my students, and I care about my friends. That hasn’t gone away.

But for quite a while now, it’s like the warmth or the drive behind things has sort of drained out of me. I’ll mean to call someone back, or go to book club, or help with theater planning, and then I just… don’t. Unless someone pushes me or reminds me, I let it slide.

I’m not proud of that. It feels lazy when I say it out loud, though I don’t think I’m trying to be. Is that what you mean by less motivated or emotionally flat?

Thinking back further, do you recall any of these changes—like feeling less motivated, more withdrawn, or having trouble keeping up with responsibilities—starting even earlier than four months ago, perhaps five or six months back?

Yes… now that you ask it that way, I think it probably did start earlier than four months ago.

I wouldn’t have called it a problem at the time, really. My youngest left for college about a year and two months ago, and I told myself it was just adjusting to the house being quieter, or a normal sort of change. But looking back, that’s when I started feeling less… connected, I suppose, and not keeping up with things quite the way I used to.

It wasn’t dramatic, and I don’t want to overstate it, but yes, the overall change has probably been going on since then. Is that helpful?
